questions.question: In an infinitely repeated game with observed actions, player $i$ uses a trigger strategy with target profile $a^c$. What does the strategy prescribe while the history shows no deviation from $a^c$?
options: Player $i$'s stage best response to the others' last actions
Player $i$'s target action $a_i^c$, in every such period
Player $i$'s part of a stage-game Nash equilibrium $a^*$
The action that punished the last deviation, kept as a warning

questions.question: In a repeated game, players use a trigger strategy with target profile $a^c$ and punishment by a stage-game Nash equilibrium $a^*$ lasting $k$ periods. What happens after the $k$ punishment periods, if nobody deviated during them?
options: Play stays at $a^*$ for the rest of the game
Play switches to the profile best for the punished player
Play stops, since the game ends after a punishment
Play returns to the target profile $a^c$

questions.question: In an infinitely repeated game, players use trigger strategies with target $a^c$ and a punishment phase. For the profile to be subgame perfect, which conditions must hold?
options: No gain from deviating on the cooperative path, and optimal play in punishment
No gain from deviating on the cooperative path; punishment play is irrelevant
Optimal play in the punishment phase; the cooperative path can be ignored
The target $a^c$ must be a stage-game Nash equilibrium

questions.question: A trigger strategy in a repeated game switches to punishment when the history shows a deviation from the target profile. Which assumption of the repeated game does this rely on?
options: That the stage game has a unique Nash equilibrium
That players discount future payoffs with $\delta<1$
That past actions are observed by all players
That players move one after another within a period

questions.question: In a repeated game, a trigger strategy aims to sustain a target profile $a^c$. In which case is a punishment phase unnecessary for sustaining $a^c$ in every period?
options: When $a^c$ is a stage-game Nash equilibrium
When $a^c$ gives every player the highest joint payoff
When the discount factor $\delta$ is close to $1$
When the punishment lasts only one period

questions.question: In a repeated stage game, player 1 has actions $X,Y,Z$; the target profile $a^c$ asks her to play $X$. Against the others' target actions she earns $4$ with $X$, $7$ with $Y$ and $5$ with $Z$. What is her one-period gain $\max_{a_1}v_1(a_1,a^c_{-1})-v_1(a^c)$?

A prisoner's dilemma has $v(C,C)=(3,3)$, $v(D,C)=(4,0)$, $v(C,D)=(0,4)$, $v(D,D)=(1,1)$ and is repeated infinitely. Players use a trigger strategy with target $(C,C)$ and a one-period punishment with $(D,D)$. For which $\delta$ does the deterrence condition $\big(v_i(a^c)-v_i(a^*)\big)(\delta+\dots+\delta^k)\ge\max_{a_i}v_i(a_i,a^c_{-i})-v_i(a^c)$ hold with $k=1$?
options: For no $\delta<1$
$\delta\ge\tfrac{1}{3}$
Every $\delta\in(0,1)$
$\delta\ge\tfrac{1}{2}$

questions.question: In a repeated prisoner's dilemma, players use a trigger strategy with target $(C,C)$ and a 2-period punishment $(D,D)$; any deviation from the prescribed profile, also during a punishment, starts a fresh 2-period punishment. Player 1 deviates in period 3 and player 2 in period 4. When does $(C,C)$ resume?
options: Period 6
Period 7
Period 5
Period 8

questions.question: Under a trigger strategy with a 3-period punishment, a deviator loses $v_i(a^c)-v_i(a^*)=2$ in each punishment period, starting one period after the deviation. With $\delta=\tfrac{1}{2}$, what is the discounted future loss $2(\delta+\delta^2+\delta^3)$?

A stage game has actions $C,D,P$ with $v(C,C)=(4,4)$, $v(D,C)=(5,0)$, $v(C,D)=(0,5)$, $v(D,D)=(1,1)$, $v(P,P)=(3,3)$, other profiles $(0,0)$. A trigger strategy targets $(C,C)$. Which punishment profile leaves no profitable deviation during punishment?
options: $(C,D)$, which gives player 1 her lowest payoff
$(P,D)$, which gives both players nothing
$(C,P)$, where both players earn $0$
$(D,D)$, a stage-game Nash equilibrium

questions.question: In a repeated game with a trigger strategy with target profile $a^c$ and punishment by a stage-game Nash equilibrium $a^*$ (any deviation restarts the punishment), why can no player gain by deviating during the punishment phase?
options: No action beats $a^*_i$ against $a^*_{-i}$, and the future cannot improve
The punishment phase is never reached, so deviations there never count
Deviations during the punishment are not observed by the other players
The deviator's punishment payoff is already the lowest she could get

questions.question: For a trigger strategy with target profile $a^c$ and punishment by a stage-game Nash equilibrium $a^*$ lasting $k$ periods, the deterrence condition $\big(v_i(a^c)-v_i(a^*)\big)(\delta+\dots+\delta^k)\ge\max_{a_i}v_i(a_i,a^c_{-i})-v_i(a^c)$ must hold. How does the smallest discount factor satisfying it change when the punishment is shortened from $k$ to $k-1$ periods?
options: It falls, since shorter punishments are more forgiving
It stays the same, since only the gain and loss matter
It rises, since the future loss is spread over fewer periods
It rises only if the deviation gain also increases

questions.question: The prisoner's dilemma with unique stage-game Nash equilibrium $(D,D)$ is repeated $T=50$ times. Can trigger strategies targeting $(C,C)$ with punishment $(D,D)$ make $(C,C)$ part of a subgame-perfect equilibrium path?
options: Yes, with a long enough punishment and $\delta$ close to $1$
Yes, in all periods except the final one
No, because $(D,D)$ is not a credible punishment
No, because the last period unravels play back to period 1

questions.question: A prisoner's dilemma has $v(C,C)=(5,5)$, $v(D,C)=(7,0)$, $v(C,D)=(0,7)$, $v(D,D)=(1,1)$, repeated infinitely. With a 2-period punishment by $(D,D)$, for which $\delta$ does the deterrence condition $\big(v_i(a^c)-v_i(a^*)\big)(\delta+\dots+\delta^k)\ge\max_{a_i}v_i(a_i,a^c_{-i})-v_i(a^c)$ hold?
options: $\delta\ge\tfrac{1}{2}$
$\delta\ge\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2}\approx0.366$
$\delta\ge\tfrac{1}{3}$
$\delta\ge\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\approx0.707$

questions.question: A repeated stage game has target $a^c$ with $v(a^c)=(3,3)$ and punishment $a^*$ with $v(a^*)=(1,1)$ for one period. Player 1's best deviation from $a^c$ pays $4$, player 2's pays $6$, and $\delta=0.9$. Does the deterrence condition $\big(v_i(a^c)-v_i(a^*)\big)(\delta+\dots+\delta^k)\ge\max_{a_i}v_i(a_i,a^c_{-i})-v_i(a^c)$ hold with $k=1$?
options: Yes, since player 1's loss $1.8$ exceeds her gain $1$
Yes, since the combined loss $3.6$ exceeds player 2's gain $3$
No, since player 2's gain $3$ exceeds her loss $1.8$
No, since one-period punishments never deter

questions.question: In the prisoner's dilemma with $v(C,C)=(3,3)$, $v(D,C)=(5,0)$, $v(D,D)=(1,1)$, repeated infinitely, players use a trigger strategy targeting $(C,C)$ with a 2-period punishment $(D,D)$ and $\delta=0.6$. Does the deterrence condition $\big(v_i(a^c)-v_i(a^*)\big)(\delta+\dots+\delta^k)\ge\max_{a_i}v_i(a_i,a^c_{-i})-v_i(a^c)$ hold?
options: No, since $2(0.6+0.36)=1.92$ is below the gain $2$
Yes, since $2(0.6+0.36)=1.92$ exceeds the gain $1.6$
Yes, since $\delta=0.6$ exceeds $\tfrac{1}{2}$
No, because the second-period loss $2\cdot0.36=0.72$ falls short of $2$

questions.question: For a trigger strategy with target profile $a^c$ and punishment by a stage-game Nash equilibrium $a^*$, the deterrence condition $\big(v_i(a^c)-v_i(a^*)\big)(\delta+\dots+\delta^k)\ge\max_{a_i}v_i(a_i,a^c_{-i})-v_i(a^c)$ depends on the punishment length $k$. Suppose that at a given $\delta<1$ the condition fails even for a punishment lasting forever ($k=\infty$). What follows for finite $k$?
options: Some finite $k$ may still work, since short punishments are credible
A finite $k$ works if it is chosen large enough
Finite $k$ always works, since forgiveness restores cooperation
No finite $k$ works, since each finite sum is below the infinite one

questions.question: In a repeated game, a trigger strategy targets $a^c$. A designer replaces the stage-game Nash equilibrium punishment $a^*$ by a harsher profile $\tilde a$ that is not a stage equilibrium. What is the effect on subgame perfection?
options: Path deterrence gets easier, but someone may gain by deviating during punishment
Both conditions get easier, since harsher punishment deters every deviation
Nothing changes, since punishments are never carried out on the path
Path deterrence gets harder, since harsher punishment lowers the future

questions.question: In the prisoner's dilemma with $v(C,C)=(3,3)$, $v(D,C)=(5,0)$, $v(D,D)=(1,1)$, repeated infinitely with $\delta=0.55$, players use a trigger strategy targeting $(C,C)$ with a $k$-period punishment $(D,D)$. What is the smallest $k$ for which the deterrence condition $\big(v_i(a^c)-v_i(a^*)\big)(\delta+\dots+\delta^k)\ge\max_{a_i}v_i(a_i,a^c_{-i})-v_i(a^c)$ holds?
options: No finite $k$

questions.question: A stage game has actions $C,D,P$ with $v(C,C)=(4,4)$, $v(D,C)=(5,0)$, $v(C,D)=(0,5)$, $v(D,D)=(1,1)$, $v(P,P)=(3,3)$, others $(0,0)$; its stage equilibria are $(D,D)$ and $(P,P)$. A trigger strategy targets $(C,C)$ with a one-period punishment. Which choice works, and for which $\delta$?
options: Either equilibrium, for $\delta\ge\tfrac{1}{3}$
Punishment $(D,D)$, for $\delta\ge\tfrac{1}{3}$
Punishment $(D,D)$, for $\delta\ge\tfrac{1}{4}$
Neither, as one-period punishments never deter
